title: Idaho's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: Idaho's 1st Congressional District covers the Idaho Panhandle and the western Boise metropolitan area. Incumbent Republican Russ Fulcher, a member of the House Freedom Caucus first elected in 2018, is seeking a fourth term in this heavily Republican district. He faces Democratic nominee Kaylee Peterson, a political strategist who previously ran for this seat in 2022 and 2024; Constitution Party nominee Brendan Gomez; and independent candidate Sarah Zabel, a retired U.S. Air Force major general. The general election is on November 3, 2026; nonpartisan analysts rate the race as Solid Republican, and District voters supported Donald Trump by approximately 45 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to this race were found. Nonpartisan analysts (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) all rate the race as Safe/Solid Republican, reflecting the district's strong Republican lean.

candidates.name: Russ Fulcher
candidates.summary: Russ Fulcher is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Idaho's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A conservative member of the House Freedom Caucus, he previously served in the Idaho Senate from 2005 to 2014 and worked in the technology industry at Micron Technology and as a commercial real estate broker. He holds a BBA and MBA from Boise State University.

candidates.name: Kaylee Peterson
candidates.summary: Kaylee Peterson is a 36-year-old working mother and sixth-generation Idahoan from Eagle, running as the Democratic nominee for Idaho's 1st Congressional District. A political strategist who previously ran for this seat in 2022 and 2024, she is a student at the College of Western Idaho studying criminal justice and political science and a nationally champion speech and debate competitor. Her campaign focuses on government accountability, banning congressional stock trades, campaign finance reform, and protecting public lands.

candidates.name: Sarah Zabel
candidates.summary: Sarah Zabel is an independent candidate for Idaho's 1st Congressional District and a retired U.S. Air Force major general with 31 years of service. A graduate of the U.S. Air Force Academy with a degree in computer science, she served in command roles including as Vice Director of the Defense Information Systems Agency. Her campaign emphasizes fiscal responsibility, health care cost reduction, preserving public lands, and immigration reform, and she positions herself as a centrist independent outside the two-party system.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists, reducing confidence and requiring reliance on structural factors. Those factors overwhelmingly favor Republicans: incumbent Russ Fulcher is seeking a fourth term in a district rated Safe/Solid Republican by all major nonpartisan analysts (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball), and Donald Trump carried the district by roughly 45 points in 2024. The Democratic nominee, Kaylee Peterson, has run twice before without any evidence of a shift toward competitiveness. The Constitution Party nominee and independent candidate Sarah Zabel (retired USAF major general) do not appear to have the campaign infrastructure or demonstrated support to make the race genuinely competitive. Given the district's strong partisan baseline, incumbent advantage, and absence of any countervailing structural factors, Republicans retain an overwhelming advantage.
